sections.h2: Why does the size of Galloway Township, NJ matter to a house seller?
sections.html:
Galloway Township is the largest municipality in New Jersey by area, so two houses with the same Galloway address can sit miles apart and attract very different buyers. Total area is 114.49 square miles, of which 88.67 are land and 25.82 are water.

The Census Bureau estimates 38,380 residents for July 2025, up from 37,813 at the 2020 census. That is a density of only 426.5 people per square mile, compared with 15,469 in Garfield, Bergen County. Galloway serves as a growing edge city to neighboring Atlantic City.

For 2020-2024 the Census Bureau shows 79.8% owner-occupied housing, a median home value of $298,900 and median gross rent of $1,619. Residents aged 65 and over make up 21.6% of the population.

sections.h2: How did Galloway Township develop, and which communities do buyers search?
sections.html:
Galloway began as a royal grant and was later divided into many smaller towns. A royal patent from King George III created the township on April 4, 1774, when it belonged to Gloucester County, and the legislature incorporated it on February 21, 1798. After Atlantic County formed in 1837, pieces were cut away to create Mullica Township, Egg Harbor City, Absecon, Brigantine and Port Republic.

The township now has no single downtown. Census-designated places inside it are Absecon Highlands, Cologne, Germania, Leeds Point, Oceanville, Pomona (7,416 residents in 2020), Smithville (7,242) and the Stockton University campus area. Other place names, including Higbeetown, Pinehurst and Somersville, show up in older deeds.

Galloway borders Absecon, Atlantic City, Egg Harbor City, Egg Harbor Township, Hamilton Township, Mullica Township and Port Republic in Atlantic County, plus Bass River and Washington townships in Burlington County and Little Egg Harbor in Ocean County. A buyer shopping for a Galloway address often compares it with houses in those towns.

sections.h2: What inspection does Galloway Township require when a house is resold?
sections.html:
Galloway requires a fire certificate on every residential resale, covering smoke detectors, carbon monoxide detectors and fire extinguishers only. Township code Chapter 153 says the inspection must happen before the new owners can occupy the dwelling.

The application, inspection and certificate go through the Fire Department at 300 E. Jimmie Leeds Road. The fee depends on how much notice you give, so ask for the inspection as soon as you have a closing date.

Galloway Township fire certificate fees by notice before change of ownership
When the request is receivedFee
More than 10 business days before the change of ownership$45
Four to 10 business days before$90
Fewer than four business days before$161

Violating the ordinance can bring a fine of up to $2,000, up to 90 days in jail or community service, and each day counts as a separate offense. Unlike Freehold Township, Galloway's resale inspection does not cover the rest of the house, since the ordinance limits it to the three fire safety items.

sections.h2: What does Galloway Township ask of an owner who rents out the house?
sections.html:
Rentals follow a separate and fuller inspection than resales. Under Galloway's rental ordinance, a certificate of occupancy is required on any rental, renewed every year or at each new occupant, whichever comes first, at $50 per inspection.

  • The lease must accompany the application and list every occupant's name and age.
  • Smoke and carbon monoxide detectors are required in every rental unit.
  • A detached one- or two-family rental needs a fire extinguisher of at least 2A:10B:C and at most 10 pounds, mounted within 10 feet of the kitchen with its top no higher than five feet from the floor.
  • A rental with a fireplace needs a chimney certification and proof that the dryer vent has been cleaned, or a notarized letter from the owner.
  • More than two follow-up inspections trigger another $50 fee.

The Housing Department handles applications at (609) 652-3700, extensions 241 or 249. Inspection requests themselves must now be emailed to the Construction office at inspect@gtnj.org with the permit number, address, type of inspection and your phone number.

sections.h2: How do the Pinelands and past storms affect a Galloway Township house?
sections.html:
Much of Galloway lies inside a protected landscape, and some parcels carry extra rules. The township is one of 56 South Jersey municipalities in the Pinelands National Reserve, a 1.1 million acre area Congress established in 1978, and parts of Galloway also fall in the state-designated Pinelands Area. Ask the Community Development office whether your parcel is in that area before you promise a buyer an addition or a new outbuilding.

Weather history is part of the picture too. In spring 2007 gypsy moth caterpillars defoliated a large swath of oak and other hardwoods in the township, and the township did not apply for state spraying that year. Tropical Storm Irene made its second U.S. landfall at Brigantine on August 28, 2011, next to Galloway.

The Community Development Department says the homeowner, not the contractor, is responsible for obtaining a permit. Residential contractors need a state Consumer Affairs 13VH number, so keep contractor names and permit numbers for any work you did before selling.

sections.h2: What do nonresident and out-of-state owners owe on a Galloway Township sale?
sections.html:
A nonresident seller prepays estimated gross income tax at the closing table. The state's formula multiplies the gain by 10.75%, but the payment can never be below 2% of the consideration written in the deed, even if there is no gain.

On a $300,000 deed, the floor works out to $6,000. The payment goes with the deed and the GIT/REP-1 form to the Atlantic County Clerk, who forwards it to the state. A seller who wants to avoid delays can prepay at a Division of Taxation regional office and receive a stamped GIT/REP-2 before closing.

  • A New Jersey resident signs the GIT/REP-3 instead and pays nothing up front.
  • A nonresident can still use the GIT/REP-3 if one of its listed assurances fits, such as a deed for $1,000 or less or a settlement with no net proceeds to the seller.
  • Selling a principal residence that qualifies under Internal Revenue Code section 121 is another listed assurance, when the entire gain can be excluded.

The Division of Taxation's GIT/REP Unit answers questions at 609-322-9275, and the Division suggests contacting it at least two weeks before a complicated closing.

sections.h2: How do schools, the Parkway and Stockton University influence Galloway Township buyers?
sections.html:
Buyers care about the Garden State Parkway and the schools. The Parkway runs 5.7 miles through the township, with Interchange 40 for U.S. Route 30, Interchange 41 for Jimmie Leeds Road and Interchange 44 for Pomona. Route 50 and County Routes 561, 563 and 575 also cross the township, and NJ Transit buses 508, 554 and 559 reach Atlantic City. The mean commute is 23.6 minutes.

Galloway Township Public Schools serve pre-K through grade 8 in six schools, with 3,164 students in 2021-22. High school students attend Absegami High School, in the township, as part of the Greater Egg Harbor Regional High School District, and families in the western part may choose Cedar Creek High School in Egg Harbor City.

Stockton University sits in the Pomona section, and Atlantic Cape Community College, with campuses in Mays Landing, Atlantic City and Cape May Court House, serves the county. A house bought as a rental brings the inspection rules above into play.

faqs.q: Does Galloway Township require an inspection to sell a house?
faqs.a: Yes, a fire certificate. Galloway requires an inspection of smoke detectors, carbon monoxide detectors and fire extinguishers on every residential resale, and it must be done before the new owners occupy the home.

faqs.q: What does the Galloway Township resale fire certificate cost?
faqs.a: It costs $45 when the request arrives more than 10 business days before the change of ownership, $90 for four to 10 business days, and $161 for fewer than four business days.

faqs.q: Where do I apply for the Galloway Township fire certificate?
faqs.a: The application, inspection and certificate are handled by the Fire Department at 300 E. Jimmie Leeds Road. The township's Housing Department can be reached at (609) 652-3700, extensions 241 or 249.

faqs.q: How much tax does a nonresident owe when selling in Galloway Township?
faqs.a: At least 2% of the deed consideration is prepaid at closing as estimated New Jersey gross income tax. The actual figure can be higher, since the formula uses the gain times 10.75%, and the seller can claim a refund after filing a nonresident return.

faqs.q: Is Galloway Township in the Pinelands?
faqs.a: Yes, in part. Galloway is within the Pinelands National Reserve, and parts of it are in the state-designated Pinelands Area. Ask the township's Community Development office about your specific parcel.
